---
title: "Workflow keepalive"
description: "Keeps scheduled workflows from being disabled after 60 days of inactivity."
---

GitHub disables a repository's scheduled workflows after **60 days without
activity** in it — for example the monthly [sweeps](suggestions.qmd#sweeps)
or a scheduled [R CMD check](r-cmd-check.qmd) in a package that isn't
changed for a while. They then silently stop running.

`workflow-keepalive.yml` re-enables the workflow that calls it, which
resets that timer. It wraps
[liskin/gh-workflow-keepalive](https://github.com/liskin/gh-workflow-keepalive),
so the action is maintained in one place instead of in every repository.

## Example

Add this job to **each workflow that has a `schedule`** trigger:

```yaml
  keepalive:
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
    permissions:
      actions: write
    uses: FlorianSchw/package-workflows/.github/workflows/workflow-keepalive.yml@main
```

The example callers of the [roxygen](roxygen-suggest.qmd) and
[test](test-coverage-suggest.qmd) suggestions already include it. It only
runs on scheduled runs, so it adds nothing to pull requests.
